lesson.subtitle: Lesson 11 -- Arriving in Australia
lesson.title_tag: Professor View -- Renato | Lesson 11 -- Arriving in Australia

listenings.text: Morning everyone, and welcome. Quick orientation, five minutes, then you are free. First, the timetable. You have six subjects and every one of them is on the sheet in your folder. Second, uniform. Yes, you have to wear it, yes, every day, and no, nobody likes it. Third, the canteen opens at half past twelve and it closes at one fifteen, so do not be late. And the one thing I say to every exchange student who has just arrived: sunscreen. Every day, even when it is cloudy. Half of you have never lived with this sun and it will find you.

So you just got here? Right, I have been here for five weeks, so let me save you some time. I have made every mistake already. I have missed the bus twice, I have turned up to the wrong classroom, and I have gone to the canteen at one twenty, which is closed. Also, I have never seen anybody eat lunch alone here, so just sit down at any table, nobody cares. And do not worry about the accent. I did not understand a word in the first week. Now I understand about eighty per cent, which is enough.

items.situation: A new classmate asks: "Have you ever been to Australia before?" Answer, and add one more fact.
Name three things you have never done in your life.
Somebody asks if you have met your roommate yet. Answer and describe him.
Ask three "Have you ever...?" questions to somebody you just met.
Somebody asks what you did last weekend. Careful: that one has a date.
